messages.subject: drawing from multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Hi Nimble team, 

I have an issue drawing from a multivariate normal distribution. I am using the following code:

my.model = nimbleCode({
  k[1:10]~dmnorm(mu_k[1:10],cov=cov_mat[1:10,1:10])
  for(j in 1:N){
    for(i in 1:n[j]){
      p[i + indOffset[j]]~dbeta(a,b)
      m[i + indOffset[j]]~T(dnorm(0.0,sd=m_sd),0.0,)
      muA[i + indOffset[j]]<- p[i + indOffset[j]]*m[i + indOffset[j]]/k[i + indOffset[j]]
      A[i + indOffset[j]]~T(dnorm(muA[i + indOffset[j]],sd=uA[i + indOffset[j]]),0,)
    }
  }
})


Each time I run the markov chain I fail to get any samples from the posterior for k. All the samples are the same value.

I have tried the following to get this to work:

  • different parameterizations
  • changing the covariance matrix
  • changing the mean vector
Any idea on what I am doing wrong, and how I can fix my issue? 

Best, 
Felix

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: drawing from multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Hi Felix,

It may be that the default RW_block sampler assigned to 'k' is
proposing "bad" values and is unable to move from its initial value. A
few things to consider:

1) Make sure to provide good initial values for all parameters

2) Test whether you can get any acceptances by setting the initial
proposal scale for the sampler for 'k' to be very small, in which case
proposals
should be accepted (but will of course not move very far).

You can do something like:
conf <- configureMCMC(model)
conf$removeSamplers('k[1:10]')
conf$addSampler('k[1:10]', 'RW_block', control = list(scale = 1e-8))
# then build and run your MCMC as usual

3) You might try the 'AF_slice' sampler in place of the 'RW_block'.
See help(samplers) for more details on this sampler.

Chris

Felix, I suspect this has to do with bad initial values in the model.

I would suggest trying model$calculate() once you've created the model object (but before anything with the MCMC).  If this returns NA, then that's almost certainly your problem.  By providing valid initial values for the model (such that model$calculate() returns a real number), the MCMC will be able to get started.

Hi again, 

I appreciate all of your help, and the quick responses. 

I have done the following so far:

1.) provided reasonable initial values for all parameters
2.) decreased the scale to 1e-8
3.) switched to AF_slice sampler


Unfortunately none of these have worked yet. When I perform model$calculate() I get a large negative number suggesting that the model is at least initialized. However, I am still not getting any samples when using the RW_block sampler (regardless of the scale), and when using the AF_slice sampler I am getting very large negative values that do not make any sense given my priors/data. I know that the model is well formulated because I can get reasonable samples in BUGS with an identical model. I'm not quite sure what to do, so I am sorry for not having any useful suggestions or questions. Do you have any more ideas on what I can look at?

Best, 
Felix

messages.subject: Re: drawing from multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Felix, we'd be happy to take a look and see what's happening, but I think to really diagnose it would require a reproducible example.  I'm especially curious about it because of the symptoms you describe: BUGS working fine, the RW_block sampler not transitioning, and the AFSS sampler giving incorrect results.

If you're more comfortable sharing a full example off the main users group list, that's fine too, of course.  But short of that, I'm not sure what to suggest.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: drawing from multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Another suggestion here is to use R's debugging tools on the
uncompiled version of the MCMC. If you set the proposal scale for the
RW_block sampler to be a very small value and step through that
sampler's first (or first few) iteration(s), you may be able to see
why no proposals are being accepted.

Suppose 'mcmc' is the uncompiled MCMC. You should be able to do
something like "debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[2]]$run)", assuming that
the 2nd sampler is your RW_block sampler. Then just start running the
MCMC (via mcmc$run) and the debugger will let you step through the
RW_block sampler steps one by one.

Chris
